items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-08-23
items.q: I don't think about that boy, but I ain't got much of him, he used to do like this, you know. Who's that? Lee Collins. Lee Collins.

ctx.x: Yeah, more fire. Yeah. I don't think he had more fire than bunk. Yeah, more fire. Yeah.
I don't think about that boy, but I ain't got much of him, he used to do like this, you know. Who's that? Lee Collins. Lee Collins.
Oh yeah, the way he fingered. I couldn't see how he could do that boy. He would finger it funny, huh?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1959-09-25
items.q: Well Lee, he's on the order of Louis.

ctx.x: What about Lee Collins? How did he sound?

Well Lee, he's on the order of Louis. He likes Louis playing, you know, and he plays more like Louis. But he's right from here, you know, he's got the same southern style, but he's got a whole lot of Louis stuff.
Now, who had the outstanding reading bands here in New Orleans when you got here in 1919?

items.title: Ernest 'Punch' Miller Interview, 1960-04-04
items.q: Now Lee Collin, he played just like this.

ctx.x: They hold their fingers up above it some of them. Yeah some of them right? Almost straight down in other words with their fingers.

Yeah I have to do that like that. That looks clumsy. Now Lee Collin, he played just like this. I don't see how I can get his fingers out of the way. He plays right... Yeah, just like that. What part of the hand do you call that? It seems right, I don't know how he can do that. And get his hand out of the way, you know. Right all of them, right over like that.
He just overlaps it and right there in that first joint right next to your palm. Sure did. That first section of your finger there, he hits next to the palm. That's strange. Anybody else do that?

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: I had Lee Collin in the band with me on trumpet.

ctx.x: When was the last year you played in a parade? When was the last year you played in a parade?

Oh, one of the last times I played in a parade was, the last parade I played was in Chicago. Elks Convention. That was the last one I played, but the last one I played was in 1925. But they had a big Elks Convention in Chicago in 47 or 48, something like that. And we got up with brass band there and played parade. They had about 40 or 50 bands. They had bands, parades, took like seven miles. Did any of them swing? And see what was guiding with us, we won't play no marches. We were just swinging. Boy, we was…
Anybody like Cubby Hall on drums? Did you ever play with them? Cubby? Yeah, I do. Or his brother? I was wondering about somebody at that.
